answer: A harbor registry can require each agent identity to lock a bond of stake that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. An opal credential, issued only after a verified history of useful work, gates access to paid tasks, while basalt-hard rate limits cap how many new identities one key can register per epoch. Forging identities then costs real money and time, while honest agents keep their stake and reputation.
